name: Hotel des Indes
insider_take: This grand dame has been The Hague's most prestigious address since 1858, where royalty, diplomats, and cultural icons have written history within its elegant walls.
whats_special: Hotel des Indes is the only hotel in The Hague where you can literally walk to three royal palaces. Originally built as a mansion for Baron van Brienen, it became legendary when Mata Hari was arrested here in 1917. The hotel's famous Le Restaurant serves afternoon tea in the same ballroom where international peace treaties have been celebrated.
pro_tip: Book the Anna Pavlova Suite—the Russian ballerina stayed here so often they named it after her, and it features original 19th-century moldings with modern luxury touches.
dont_miss: The hotel's signature high tea experience in the stunning ballroom, and take the 5-minute walk to the Binnenhof, where you can tour the medieval castle that houses the Dutch Parliament. The nearby Mauritshuis museum showcases Vermeer's "Girl with a Pearl Earring."
pros: Historic luxury palace hotel with 19th-century grandeur
Prime location in The Hague's cultural and political district
Exceptional service standards from Leading Hotels of the World
Elegant rooms and suites with classic European sophistication
cons: Premium pricing reflective of luxury positioning
Traditional formal atmosphere may not suit casual travelers
